questions.question: A solid cuboid is built out of 1 cm cubes with no gaps. It is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume of a rectangular prism is length x width x height, so 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 cubic centimetres (the 4 x 3 = 12 cubes in the bottom layer, repeated for 2 layers). The common trap is answering 52, which is the surface area — the amount of skin on the outside, measured in square centimetres, not the space inside.

questions.question: A solid cuboid is made from 1 cm cubes. Its length is 5 cm, its width is 2 cm and its height is 3 cm. How much space does it take up?
questions.explain: Multiply all three measurements: 5 x 2 x 3 = 30 cubic centimetres. Answering 10 uses only the bottom layer (5 x 2) and forgets to repeat it 3 times; answering 62 gives the surface area instead of the volume.

questions.question: A solid cuboid stack of 1 cm cubes measures 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 5 cm high. What is the volume of the whole stack?
questions.explain: One layer holds 6 x 4 = 24 cubes, and there are 5 layers, so 24 x 5 = 120 cubic centimetres. Stopping at 24 gives only the area of the base, and 148 is the surface area — volume always uses all three measurements.

questions.question: A solid cuboid is a perfect cube: every edge is 4 cm long. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Even for a cube the rule is the same: 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 cubic centimetres. The trap here is 96, which is the surface area (6 faces of 16 square centimetres each) — surface area is measured in square units, volume in cubic units.

questions.question: A rectangular prism has l = 8 cm, w = 5 cm and h = 4 cm. Find V.
questions.explain: Use V = l x w x h: 8 x 5 = 40 for the base, then 40 x 4 = 160 cubic centimetres. Answering 184 means the surface-area formula was used by mistake, and 17 comes from adding the three measurements instead of multiplying them.

questions.question: A gift box shaped like a rectangular prism has a volume of 120 cubic centimetres. Its base is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. How tall is the box?
questions.explain: Since V = l x w x h, first find the base: 6 x 4 = 24 square centimetres, then 120 divided by 24 = 5 cm. The usual slip is dividing by just one measurement (120 divided by 6 = 20), which ignores the other side of the base.

questions.question: Maya has a rectangular fish tank that is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 25 cm high. Filled right to the top, what is its capacity in litres? (1 litre = 1000 cubic centimetres)
questions.explain: First find the volume: 30 x 20 x 25 = 15 000 cubic centimetres, then divide by 1000 to get 15 litres. The trap is the conversion — dividing by 100 or 10 000 instead of 1000 gives 150 or 1.5.

questions.question: A box of granola bars from a Surrey grocery store is 20 cm long, 10 cm wide and 6 cm high. How much space is inside the box?
questions.explain: Multiply 20 x 10 x 6 = 1200 cubic centimetres. The word 'box' tempts people into 760, the surface area of the cardboard; the space inside is volume, so all three measurements must be multiplied.

questions.question: Jonah is choosing a storage bin for his hockey gear. The blue bin is 12 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm and the green bin is 10 cm x 6 cm x 4 cm (measured on a model). Which bin holds more?
options: They hold the same amount: 240 cubic centimetres each
The blue bin, because it has more material around it: 256 square centimetres against 248
The blue bin, because its longest side is 12 cm
The green bin, because 6 cm is wider than 5 cm
questions.explain: Work out each volume: 12 x 5 x 4 = 240 and 10 x 6 x 4 = 240, so the bins hold exactly the same amount. Two prisms can have equal volume but different surface areas, so comparing the outside material — or just the longest side — does not tell you which holds more.

questions.question: An aquarium at Ella's school is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm high. The class fills it with water to a depth of 20 cm. How much water is in the aquarium? (1 litre = 1000 cubic centimetres)
questions.explain: The water itself is a rectangular prism 40 cm x 25 cm x 20 cm, so 40 x 25 x 20 = 20 000 cubic centimetres, which is 20 litres. The trap is using the height of the tank (30 cm) instead of the depth of the water, which measures the empty tank rather than what is in it.

questions.question: Nadia works out the volume of a box that is 10 cm x 4 cm x 3 cm. She writes 2 x (40 + 30 + 12) = 164. Which statement is correct?
options: Nadia is right; the volume is 164 cubic centimetres
Nadia is right, but she should write 164 square centimetres
Nadia found the surface area; the volume is 120 cubic centimetres
Nadia should have added the measurements to get 17 cubic centimetres
questions.explain: Volume is length x width x height: 10 x 4 x 3 = 120 cubic centimetres. Nadia used 2 x (lw + lh + wh), which totals the six faces — that is surface area in square centimetres, the space around the box rather than the space inside it.

questions.question: Dad builds a rectangular planter box for the backyard that is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 20 cm deep. Soil is sold in 9 litre bags. How many bags are needed to fill the planter completely? (1 litre = 1000 cubic centimetres)
questions.explain: Volume first: 60 x 30 x 20 = 36 000 cubic centimetres, which is 36 litres, then 36 divided by 9 = 4 bags. Two traps hide here — stopping at 36 forgets that each bag holds 9 litres, and using the surface area of the wood instead of the space inside gives a much smaller, wrong amount of soil.
